allowance_taper.source: GOV.UK, Income Tax rates and allowances for current and previous tax years: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/rates-and-allowances-income-tax/income-tax-rates-and-allowances-current-and-past

scottish_bands_note: Amounts of taxable income above the personal allowance (gross: starter £12,571-£16,537, basic to £29,526, intermediate to £43,662, higher to £75,000, advanced to £125,140). Agreed by the Scottish Parliament on 19 February 2026 (motion S6M-20844).
scottish_bands_source: GOV.UK, Rates and thresholds for employers 2026 to 2027: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/rates-and-thresholds-for-employers-2026-to-2027; gov.scot, Scottish Income Tax rates and bands 2026 to 2027: https://www.gov.scot/publications/scottish-income-tax-rates-and-bands/pages/2026-to-2027/; Scottish Parliament motion S6M-20844: https://www.parliament.scot/chamber-and-committees/votes-and-motions/S6M-20844

national_insurance.source: GOV.UK, Rates and thresholds for employers 2026 to 2027 (Class 1, category A): https://www.gov.uk/guidance/rates-and-thresholds-for-employers-2026-to-2027

nhs_scotland_pension_note: Tiers are on actual pensionable pay, not whole-time equivalent. 'tiers' is Table 2 (new starters and in-year pay changes, on current annualised pay); 'continuing' is Table 1 (members tiered on 2025/26 pay). Employers apply these under Circular 2026/03; the amending regulations are expected in force from 9 December 2026, backdated to 1 April 2026.
nhs_scotland_pension_source: SPPA NHS Circular 2026/03, Employee contribution tier bandings from 1 April 2026: https://pensions.gov.scot/sites/default/files/2026-03/2026_03_-_NHS_Employee_contribution_tier_bandings_from_1_April_2026.pdf

high_income_child_benefit_charge.note: 1% of Child Benefit repaid for every £200 of adjusted net income over £60,000; all of it from £80,000.
high_income_child_benefit_charge.source: GOV.UK, High Income Child Benefit Charge: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit-tax-charge

tax_free_childcare.note: The government adds £2 for every £8 paid in, up to £500 a quarter (£2,000 a year) per child. Each parent must expect to earn at least £2,643.68 over the next 3 months (21 and over).

funded_childcare.note: From the term after the third birthday until school. Councils set the actual term dates (August, January, March or April); the month here is the usual one. Some 2-year-olds qualify too (certain benefits, or care experience), from the same windows.
funded_childcare.source: mygov.scot, Funded early learning and childcare: https://www.mygov.scot/childcare-costs-help/funded-early-learning-and-childcare; SSI 2014/196 art. 1: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ssi/2014/196/article/1
